title: AI Daily Briefing
description: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, open and local models, and AI in defense.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 16–24. New: Anthropic said Nov. 23 that Claude Ship is in beta for Team and Enterprise GitHub repositories, and Google said the same day that Search AI Mode can connect Google Wallet, with Drive and the Gemini app to follow. OpenAI and Cisco's Shirudo runtime is on the cyber page. No new Nvidia model post dated Nov. 23–24 was opened beyond the board's reinstatement of Jensen Huang, which is on the partners page. The Open and Local Models subsection is empty.

items.headline: Anthropic opens Claude Ship in beta to review, fix, and approve pull requests
items.summary: Anthropic said Nov. 23 that Claude Ship is available in beta on Team and Enterprise plans for GitHub repositories. Anthropic said Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta, and that Claude Approvals applies a policy the team writes as a file in the repository. Anthropic recommends running approvals in observe-only mode first, and said administrators can set spend limits for Code Review and PR Steward. Anthropic said Claude Ship is not available to organizations with zero data retention, a HIPAA configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys.

items.headline: Anthropic opens Claude computer use in beta for Team and Enterprise plans
items.summary: Anthropic's Nov. 20 release notes say computer use is available in beta on Team and Enterprise plans and is rolling out gradually. Anthropic's admin guide says the control is off by default, that Claude can see a user's screen and work in the desktop apps the user allows, and that there is no sandbox between Claude and those applications. The guide says computer use is not limited to folders a user has connected, that marking a folder read-only does not apply, and that organizations with a HIPAA-ready configuration, zero data retention for Claude Code, customer-managed encryption keys, or FERPA or K-12 settings cannot turn it on. Anthropic says screenshots used to navigate the screen are saved with the chat and can include confidential information.

items.headline: Anthropic shares closed their first day at $97.17, up from an $83 IPO price
items.summary: Anthropic said Nov. 18 that it priced its initial public offering at $83.00 per share and that the shares were expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19 under the symbol ANT. CNBC reported that the shares opened at $111.50 and closed the first session at $97.17, and that more than 846 million shares changed hands. CNBC said Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the offering and that the fully diluted market capitalization at the close was roughly $1.8 trillion. Anthropic said the offering is expected to close Nov. 20, subject to customary conditions, and that the company is selling 956,351,354 of the 980,000,000 shares.

items.headline: OpenAI says its models improved AMD's flagship GPU design by up to 14 percent
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 18 that its models produced up to a 14 percent improvement in power, performance, and area against heavily optimized baselines on AMD's flagship GPU intellectual property by rewriting SystemVerilog. OpenAI said that was about a year of progress in less than five months, that AMD included some changes in a design sent for manufacturing, and that AMD verified single-digit percentage gains on key blocks of its next flagship CPU. OpenAI said it is partnering with Synopsys to train a model, GPT-Synopsys, on Synopsys design tools. Tom's Hardware reported those findings on Nov. 20.

items.headline: OpenAI's MedChemBench scores GPT-6.2 Astra at 84.5 percent
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 20 that MedChemBench tests whether models can connect a molecule's structure with experimental evidence, using 99 problems drawn from 117 papers and patents and 761 distinct structures. OpenAI said that at the xhigh reasoning setting GPT-6.2 Astra earned 84.5 percent of the available credit, compared with 83.3 percent for GPT-6 Astra, 82.0 percent for GPT-6.1 Sol, and 58.2 percent for GPT-5.6 Sol. OpenAI said GPT-6 Astra was strongest at reconstructing structures and explaining evidence, and that selecting compounds and predicting numerical properties earned only about half the credit for Astra at that setting. OpenAI said the results do not show that models can discover drugs, that prior exposure to the published sources cannot be ruled out, and that each response was a single attempt without tools or new experiments.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, with a cyber track for the Fairwind Program
items.summary: Google said Nov. 18 that Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out in the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Gemini for business, Google Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers. Google said the price is $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 per million cached input tokens, and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window. Google said Neon scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level, and that at the default high thinking level it costs 32 percent less per task than Gemini 4 Carbon on that index. Google said Neon for cyber is state of the art on SEC-bench Pro at 90.5 percent and on WebExploitBench v1.2 at 51.26 percent, and that eligible Fairwind Program members will begin receiving access over the next few days.

items.headline: Google lets Search AI Mode connect Wallet, with Drive and Gemini next
items.summary: Google said Nov. 23 that people can opt in to connect Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, and that Drive and the Gemini app will follow in the coming weeks. Google said those connections join Gmail, Calendar, and Photos. Google said AI Mode can only read Wallet information and cannot move, manage, or invest money. Google said users turn connections on or off in Search Personalization, and that AI Overviews and AI Mode will also use recent search context unless personalization is turned off.

items.headline: Nvidia says it has agreed to acquire Hugging Face as Vera Rubin ships
items.summary: NVIDIA said Nov. 17, in its fiscal 2027 third-quarter release, that it has agreed to acquire Hugging Face to scale that platform. The same release said Vera Rubin NVL72 has begun shipping, which NVIDIA called the fastest product ramp in its history, with racks running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and Nebius, and coming online soon at SpaceXSI. NVIDIA said it expanded Anthropic's access to Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity through cloud providers.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: China says it will answer the new AI-chip rental controls
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 18 that China's Ministry of Commerce said China will take countermeasures to safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests after the United States extended export controls on high-end AI accelerator chips. Tom's Hardware said the updated regulation requires licenses to rent those chips in large quantities to Country Group D:5, the list of nations embargoed from arms sales. Tom's Hardware said President Trump is in China for the APEC summit in Shenzhen and is scheduled to meet President Xi Jinping on Nov. 19.

items.headline: BIS issues a rule on remote access to advanced chips through overseas data centers
items.summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security said Nov. 16 that it released an interim final rule, written at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council, so limits on advanced super-intelligence chips cannot be bypassed through remote computing at data centers in third countries. The rule text requires a license to export, reexport, or transfer covered items for a data center, anywhere, that will provide access to more than 12 million aggregate total processing performance to a company headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in, Macau or Country Group D:5. It also requires a license for advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil, with an exception for a U.S.-headquartered consignee that meets a reporting requirement, and it formally rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule, which the preamble says has never been enforced. The displayed text says the rule takes effect on the date it is published in the Federal Register.

items.headline: OpenAI says NATO is using Daybreak models to defend allied networks
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 17 that it works with NATO's Communications and Information Agency to give NATO's core institutions access to advanced cybersecurity models, and that NATO has used up to 300 billion raw input and output tokens per month in that work. OpenAI said it supported the 2026 Crossed Swords exercise, run by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence, where participants built and evaluated AI agents for cyber operations using Daybreak, with an emphasis on human oversight. OpenAI said it has also provided the models to ENISA and to national cyber agencies in France, Germany, and Poland, and that Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation is using Daybreak on civilian infrastructure. NCIA General Manager Dylan Browne said the tools accelerate vulnerability discovery and that NATO will study token consumption and cost as adoption scales.

items.headline: AFRICOM hosts Maven workshops with an Army-led edge super-intelligence team
items.summary: U.S. Africa Command said Nov. 17 that it hosted the Office of the Secretary of War's Chief Data and Analytics Office for workshops in Stuttgart with Maven users from Special Operations Command Africa and AFRICOM's Directorate of Operations. AFRICOM said Maven scans imagery and video, flags information for human analysts, and shows the battlefield on one dashboard, and that the sessions looked for near-term fixes and longer-term needs. A workshop photo is dated Nov. 12 at Kelley Barracks. Army Capt. Ryan T. Hetrick, lead of the Edge Super Intelligence Task Force at the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, said developers have to go where the warfighter works and build alongside the end user.
